check.reason: The target is the system: vendors, revenue-cycle tech hype, and prior authorization bureaucracy. Patients, authors and private individuals are not mocked, and nothing involves death, children or violence. The headline stays close to the real story, which argues that more AI is not the fix and that orchestration is. The joke, that the industry's answer is a rebrand, is dry and clearly satirical. It does not quote the article. The 4% figure is the one item to check: it is presented as fact and I could not verify it from the headline alone, so confirm it appears in the source summary before publishing.

pick.title: More AI won’t fix healthcare’s revenue cycle. Orchestration will.
pick.headline: Revenue Cycle AI Underperforms; Industry Recommends Giving It a New Name
pick.take: Only 4% of providers have connected their revenue automation, so the rest own several expensive robots that don't talk to each other. The proposed fix is a word: orchestration. Prior authorization already has a name, and it still takes a fax and a prayer.
